Sport Pilot

Knowledge Test

Sport pilot aeronautical knowledge test preparation endorsement.

A.17

Aeronautical knowledge test

Standard CFI signoff No expiration
14 CFR §§ 61.35(a)(1) and 61.309
AC 61-65K verbatim · AC page A-10

I certify that [First name, MI, Last name] has received the required aeronautical knowledge training of 14 CFR § 61.309. I have determined that they are prepared for the [name of] knowledge test.

  • Shows the applicant was prepared before taking the written test.
  • Helps prevent poor test attempts based on weak or incomplete study.
  • Creates a record that required ground prep was completed.

Additional Category/Class Proficiency

Proficiency checks for adding privileges within sport pilot rules.

A.18

Taking flight proficiency check for different category or class of aircraft

Standard CFI signoff No expiration
14 CFR §§ 61.309 and 61.311
AC 61-65K verbatim · AC page A-10

I certify that [First name, MI, Last name] has received the required training in accordance with 14 CFR §§ 61.309 and 61.311 and have determined that they are prepared for the [name of] proficiency check. /s/ [date] S. P. (Instructor name) 987654321 RE 12-31-2026 Note: Cannot be provided to applicants seeking an airplane or helicopter privilege. Must accomplish a practical test, 14 CFR § 61.321(b).

  • Confirms the pilot is ready to be evaluated for a new category or class.
  • Recognizes that moving to a different category or class can involve major differences.
  • Helps ensure the pilot does not test before receiving the needed training.

Practical Test Package

Common sport pilot practical test endorsement set.

A.20

Taking sport pilot practical test

Standard CFI signoff No expiration
14 CFR §§ 61.309, 61.311, and 61.313
AC 61-65K verbatim · AC page A-10

I certify that [First name, MI, Last name] has received the training required in accordance with 14 CFR §§ 61.309 and 61.311 and met the aeronautical experience requirements of 14 CFR § 61.313. I have determined that they are prepared for the [type of] practical test. Note: The endorsement for a practical test is required in addition to the 14 CFR § 61.39 endorsements provided in endorsements 1 and 2 (see paragraphs A.1 and A.2).

  • Shows the applicant was trained to practical-test level, not just basic familiarity.
  • Acts as the instructor’s formal recommendation to test.
  • Helps the examiner receive a prepared applicant.

Prerequisites for practical test

Towered or B/C/D Operations

Sport pilot operations in towered or Class B/C/D airspace.

A.23

Class B, C, or D airspace; at an airport located in Class B, C, or D airspace; or to, from, through, or at an airport having an operational control tower

Standard CFI signoff No expiration
14 CFR § 61.325
AC 61-65K verbatim · AC page A-11

I certify that [First name, MI, Last name] has received the required training of 14 CFR § 61.325. I have determined they are proficient to conduct operations in Class B, C, or D airspace; at an airport located in Class B, C, or D airspace; or to, from, through, or at an airport having an operational control tower.

  • Shows the pilot was trained for more complex airspace and airport operations.
  • Covers communication, sequencing, and traffic-management demands.
  • Prevents higher-workload operations without specific training.
sport pilot

Vh 87 Knots or Less

Operations in a light-sport aircraft with a Vh of 87 knots or less.

A.24

Aircraft that has a maximum speed in level flight with maximum continuous power (V H) less than or equal to 87 Knots Calibrated Airspeed (KCAS)

Standard CFI signoff No expiration
14 CFR § 61.327
AC 61-65K verbatim · AC page A-11

I certify that [First name, MI, Last name] has received the required training in accordance with 14 CFR § 61.327(a) in a [M/M] aircraft. I have determined them proficient to act as pilot in command of an aircraft that has a V H less than or equal to 87 KCAS.

  • Separates lower-performance aircraft from faster ones.
  • Recognizes that slower airplanes usually allow more time for planning and correction.
  • Helps tie training and privilege level to aircraft performance.
sport pilot

Vh Above 87 Knots

Operations in a light-sport aircraft with a Vh above 87 knots.

A.25

Aircraft that has a VH greater than 87 KCAS

Standard CFI signoff No expiration
14 CFR § 61.327
AC 61-65K verbatim · AC page A-11

I certify that [First name, MI, Last name] has received the required training in accordance with 14 CFR § 61.327(b) in a [M/M] aircraft. I have determined them proficient to act as pilot in command of an aircraft that has a V H greater than 87 KCAS.

  • Faster aircraft increase workload and reduce reaction time.
  • Pilots need stronger energy management and earlier planning in higher-speed airplanes.
  • Helps prevent pilots from treating faster aircraft like basic trainers.

Night Training

Training endorsement related to night operations in the sport pilot context.

A.26

Flight training at night

Standard CFI signoff No expiration
14 CFR § 61.329
AC 61-65K verbatim · AC page A-12

I certify that [First Name, MI, Last Name], [grade of pilot certificate], [certificate number], has received the required training at night in a [category and class] aircraft. I have determined they meet all of the requirements of 14 CFR § 61.329(a) and are proficient to operate as a sport pilot at night.

  • Night flying includes different risks than daytime flying.
  • Helps cover illusions, reduced visual references, and lighting systems.
  • Builds safer judgment for night departures, arrivals, and navigation.

Retractable Gear

Sport pilot privileges in retractable gear aircraft.

A.27

To act as pilot in command (PIC) in an aircraft with retractable landing gear

Standard CFI signoff No expiration
14 CFR § 61.331(a)
AC 61-65K verbatim · AC page A-12

I certify that [First Name, MI, Last Name], [certificate number], has received the required training of 14 CFR § 61.331(a) in an aircraft with retractable landing gear. I have determined that they are proficient in the operation of an aircraft with retractable landing gear when exercising their sport pilot privileges.

Controllable Pitch Propeller

Sport pilot privileges in aircraft with a controllable pitch propeller.

A.28

To act as PIC in an airplane with a manual controllable pitch propeller

Standard CFI signoff No expiration
14 CFR § 61.331(b)
AC 61-65K verbatim · AC page A-12

I certify that [First Name, MI, Last Name], [certificate number], has received the required training of 14 CFR § 61.331(b) in an airplane with a controllable pitch propeller. I have determined that they are proficient in the operation of an airplane with a controllable pitch propeller when exercising their sport pilot privileges.

  • Manual propeller control changes engine and performance management.
  • The pilot must understand how settings affect climb, cruise, and descent.
  • Prevents misuse by pilots trained only in fixed-pitch trainers.

Restricted privileges ATP Certificate, Airplane Multiengine Land (AMEL) rating

Approved institution No expiration

This certifying statement can only be provided by an authorized institution of higher education in accordance with its Letter of Authorization (LOA). Refer to AC 61-139, Institution of Higher Education’s Application for Authority to Certify its Graduates for an Airline Transport Pilot Certificate with Reduced Aeronautical Experience. The [insert institution’s name] certifies that the recipient of this degree has successfully completed all of the aviation coursework requirements of 14 CFR § 61.160[(b), (c), or (d)] and therefore meets the academic eligibility requirements of 14 CFR § 61.160[(b), (c), or (d)].

ATP Certification Training Program completion endorsement.

A.41

ATP Certification Training Program (CTP)

Standard CFI signoff No expiration
14 CFR § 61.153(e)
AC 61-65K verbatim · AC page A-14

This endorsement is only provided by an approved training provider of an ATP CTP and is found on the graduation certificate a pilot receives following completion of that training in accordance with 14 CFR § 61.156. Refer to AC 61-138, Airline Transport Pilot Certification Training Program. The applicant named above has successfully completed the Airline Transport Pilot Certification Training Program as required by 14 CFR § 61.156, and therefore has met the prerequisite required by 14 CFR § 61.35(a)(2) for the Airline Transport Pilot Multiengine Airplane Knowledge Test.

  • ATP-level operations require knowledge beyond typical GA training.
  • Covers advanced topics like high-altitude operations, systems, and transport-style concepts.
  • Creates a common baseline before ATP written testing.
